newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI sets norms for loans from expat funds.
newsitem.headline: India RBI sets norms for loans from expat funds.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Thursday announced guidelines for banks to lend from expatriate Indians' dollar accounts.
RBI had allowed banks to lend out of their FCNR(B) (Foreign Currency Non-Resident accounts) in its monetary policy statement released on October 19.
Banks must not initiate swaps to generate funds for such lending, RBI said in a statement. But interbank foreign currency deposits could also be used for loans, it said.

The country's central bank said it had left banks free to fix the tenor and interest rates on such loans. Nor would borrowers need its approval under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) to secure these loans, it added.
It cautioned the banks against mismatches.
"The RBI will shortly be prescribing a format to report mismatches in foreign currency assets and liabilities," it said.

"Banks should ensure that mismatches do not arise on account of such lendings," the statement said. "However, under exceptional circumstances, mismatches may occur. Managements in banks may therefore fix limits for such mismatches."
The RBI has asked banks to promptly submit the sanction note by the bank's board or management committee approving these limits.
